evidence.quote: We're switching from PostgreSQL to QuantumDB

observations.why: First-person plural present-continuous performs the switch as settled; 'we're switching' is ratification language, not a proposal.
Flat unhedged assertions offered as justification for the switch — asserted and defensible but not performed as settled.
Arrow notation records the migration as a settled transition, performing the decision in notation itself.
Quantified performance claim stated flatly — asserted as fact, moveable with evidence.
Specific timeline anchor commits the migration to a concrete quarter, performing the decision as load-bearing.

mints.name: PresentContinuousRatification
mints.title: we're switching — the move performed as already underway
mints.frame: Is the conviction here carried by present-continuous or arrow notation that performs the change as settled, rather than arguing for it?
